headline: Short-term law that keeps Federal Aviation Administration programs, funding, and aviation taxes running through March 8, 2024.
what_it_does: This law extends the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) authority to operate, spend money, and run its programs until March 8, 2024. It keeps airport improvement grants, air traffic and safety operations, drone programs, and rural air service programs going without major changes. It also continues the taxes on airline tickets and aviation fuel that pay for these programs.

who_it_affects.how: Taxes on airline tickets continue to be collected, and consumer protection and disability access advisory committees keep operating.
Airports remain eligible for federal Airport Improvement Program grants for construction, planning, noise, and land-use projects.
The Essential Air Service Program and small community air service grants continue, helping keep scheduled flights in these areas.
Taxes on aviation fuel continue, and federal aviation insurance and air traffic control services keep running.
FAA drone test sites, safety exemptions, and drone detection and enforcement programs continue.
A pause on certain federal safety rules for crewed launch vehicle design and operation continues through March 9, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: FAA employees and contract weather observers
who_it_affects.how: FAA salaries and operations remain authorized, and the FAA cannot end its contract weather observer program at any airport during the extension.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed December 26, 2023; extensions last through March 8, 2024 (March 9, 2024 for the commercial spaceflight rule pause).
